cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code constructs a shell command by directly interpolating user-controlled startTag and endTag parameters into a git diff command that is executed via child_process.exec, allowing shell metacharacters to modify command execution.

connection.evidence: startTag and endTag are function parameters passed to gitDiffApply (lines 36-37) and flow directly into the shell command at line 135 via string interpolation, with no intermediate validation or sanitization.

diff_causality.evidence: This candidate line is the vulnerable command construction. Reverting it would remove the command injection vector entirely, as the shell command execution with unsanitized input would not occur.

security_control.evidence: No validation, sanitization, or escaping of user input before shell command interpolation
security_control.required_control: Input sanitization or parameterization for shell command arguments
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-77 requires neutralization of shell metacharacters when constructing commands from external input to prevent command injection
existing_controls_checked: No input validation on startTag/endTag parameters
No escaping in the command construction
No parameterized command execution in utils.run
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The code directly interpolates user-controlled tags into shell command strings without any sanitization, allowing shell metacharacters like ;, &, |, $, and backticks to execute arbitrary commands

concrete_impact.evidence: Command injection could lead to arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the application, potentially compromising the system or exposing sensitive repository data.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the git diff command with unsanitized user input would not be executed, eliminating the command injection vulnerability at this location.
supporting_evidence: startTag and endTag are user-provided function parameters with no validation
The utils.run function uses child_process.exec which executes in a shell context
Tags are directly interpolated into the command string without escaping
The same unsanitized tags are used in multiple shell commands throughout the codebase
unresolved_facts: Whether calling code validates tags before passing to gitDiffApply
Whether tags are expected from trusted sources only
Whether there are external security controls not visible in repository
review_comment: User-controlled startTag and endTag parameters are directly interpolated into a shell command without sanitization, enabling command injection via shell metacharacters. The patch creates a git diff command that executes in a shell context, allowing attackers to inject arbitrary commands. Use parameterized command execution by passing tags as separate arguments or implement strict tag validation with allowlisting of safe characters.
